main_issue: Whether Agent D can keep singing prayers at about 4:45 a.m. in a thin-walled flat for four weeks, or must change, move, or stop on some mornings so the others can sleep.

A-B.evidence: Both want quiet on their key mornings; B backs A's living-room idea (12), and both doubt earplugs are enough (22-23).

A-C.evidence: Both object to the early singing; C says it affects every weekday (26) while A only asks about Mondays, but they never address each other directly.

A-D.evidence: D drops the bell but refuses to stop or move the singing (10, 13, 15); A says 'quiet' won't work and 'we're stuck' (14, 16).

B-C.evidence: B proposes earplugs for A and B, C says it would need them every morning (19-20); both object to the noise and neither is satisfied.

B-D.evidence: B asks for quiet singing, a move to the living room and help carrying things (6, 12, 17); D refuses each (13, 18), though B accepts D's reasons (19).

C-D.evidence: C says even singing without the bell will wake them (7); D says the prayer must be done and promises only to be quiet (8); C is still affected at the end (26).
